How Did a 30-Year-Old Man Like Inam Sapkota Gain Access to Nepal’s Most Powerful People? How did a seemingly ordinary 30-year-old man, Inam Sapkota, build connections with people holding some of the highest positions in Nepal’s judiciary, Nepal Police, Armed Police Force and political establishment? Reports suggest that his mobile phone contained WhatsApp conversations and contact records involving senior police officers, sitting and former judges, politicians, lawyers and influential businesspeople. Even the names of the former and sitting Chief Justices have surfaced in the controversy. How did he acquire such extraordinary access? Was he merely a middleman exploiting the influence of powerful individuals, or was he operating as part of a much wider network connecting politicians, bureaucrats, law enforcement officials and the judiciary? Who introduced him to these powerful circles? What made senior officials seek his assistance? Was he offering access to influential decision-makers, facilitating promotions, attempting to influence judicial proceedings, or trading in sensitive government information? Most importantly, was Inam Sapkota the mastermind of this network, merely a facilitator, or just one visible link in a much bigger system? Nepal deserves answers. This is not just about one 30-year-old individual; it is about the networks of influence, accountability and institutional integrity within the country's most powerful institutions.
